name: Self-Transcendence 2 mailin juoksu, Vaasa
description: The Self-Transcendence 2 Mile Run Vaasa takes place every Tuesday from May to September at 7:00 p.m. on the Hietalahti Peace Mile. The course is a 1-mile park route completed twice. The start and registration are behind the swimming hall. The run offers a fast and pleasant park route suitable for runners of all levels.
course_highlights: A 1-mile park route
The course is completed twice
The start and registration are behind the swimming hall
additional: Runs are held every Tuesday from May to September. The event has several age-group categories. Results from previous years are available. The event is organized by the Sri Chinmoy Marathon Team, which has served the running community for over 35 years. The event takes place every Tuesday at 7 p.m. through September, and no entry fee is specified.

name: Finlandiaviesti
location: Jyväskylä, Rantaraitti, Jyväskylä, Central Finland, Finland
description: Finlandiaviesti 1/2026 is part of the Finlandia Marathon event, held in Jyväskylä on 11–12 September 2026. The event offers runners a range of distances, including 5 km, 10 km, the half marathon and the marathon, and is suitable for runners of all levels. The route follows Jyväskylä’s Rantaraitti, which has been awarded the title of Finland’s most beautiful traffic route, offering a flat and fast running experience. The Finlandia Marathon is known for its runner-friendly course, excellent atmosphere and memorable event weekend amid the beautiful scenery of Central Finland.
course_highlights: Flat and fast route along Jyväskylä’s Rantaraitti
Route awarded the title of Finland’s most beautiful traffic route
Water stations along the route, with tables reserved for runners’ own drinks
additional: There are water stations along the route, with tables for runners’ own drinks beside them. Students receive a €10 discount on the entry fee (€5 for the Finlandia Vitosella). An S-Etukortti or Juoksijakortti gives a €4 discount on the entry fee. Cancellation protection is included for registrations made by 31.5; after that, the cancellation protection fee is €5. The event includes relays, the marathon, the half marathon and shorter races, giving participants the chance to enjoy the beautiful surroundings and great atmosphere.

name: Tahko Trail Run
organizer: Kuopio-Tahko Markkinointi Oy ja TAHKOcom Oy
description: Tahko Trail Run is a new trail running event held amid the stunning scenery of Tahkovuori on 12 September 2026. The event offers four distances to choose from, suitable for both first-timers and experienced trail runners. The routes pass through varied landscapes close to nature, with heart-pumping climbs and breathtaking views. The event focuses on memorable experiences, atmosphere, well-marked routes and aid stations. The finish area offers a race-day atmosphere, food, and the chance to use the sauna and shower at Break Sokos Hotel Tahko.
course_highlights: The 8.5 km route features Tahko’s most beautiful natural attractions and scenery, and is also suitable for walking.
The 14 km route offers a challenge and memorable experiences, with approximately 370 m of elevation gain.
The challenging yet rewarding 23 km route follows the trails of Rahasmäki and includes the legendary Tahko Stairs, with approximately 650 m of elevation gain.
additional: The routes are well marked, and there are several aid stations offering water, sports drinks, fruit and salty snacks. Drinks are served only into your own container, so bringing your own cup or water bottle is recommended. Participants receive a medal as a keepsake at the finish, and light snacks and drinks are available in the finish area. The meal is a pasta buffet at Break Sokos Hotel Tahko. Participants can use the hotel’s shower and sauna. Bib collection and the information desk are located at Hophaus Tahko, next to the event area. The cloakroom is self-service and is not continuously supervised. There is plenty of parking, but most spaces are paid; free parking is available beside Tahkonlahti beach, about a 10-minute walk from the event area. The event includes drinks, a pasta buffet at Break Sokos Hotel Tahko, and access to the hotel’s shower and sauna. Children and families can also participate.

name: SaaristoTrail
description: SaaristoTrail is an exciting trail-running event in Parainen, offering varied routes through stunning archipelago scenery. The event has three main distances: 7 km, 14 km and a 21 km half marathon, suitable for both beginners and more experienced trail runners. The routes include varied trails, forest tracks and significant elevation changes, including the steep climbs of Svinövuori, offering unforgettable views and a challenge. The relaxed atmosphere and careful organization make it an enjoyable experience for all participants.
course_highlights: Varied trails and forest tracks
Steep climbs up Svinövuori, with juice served at the summit
Approximately 850 metres of total ascent on the 21 km route
additional: The 1 km children's run is free for those who register in advance (the last day to register is 10.9) and costs 5 euros for late registration. All children taking part receive a medal. The event centre is at Finby Ski Stadium, where shower facilities are also available in the changing rooms at Archipelagia Golf. The route is marked with red-and-white plastic tape. Race materials can be collected from the race office starting at 8.45 and up to half an hour before your start. Juice and water are available at the finish, and the results are posted on the information board. Late registration at the event venue is available via MobilePay or bank card; cash is not accepted. The event offers different route options, so participants can choose a suitable distance. Routes and results are available on the event website, and the event offers a chance to enjoy the archipelago’s natural scenery and the joy of exercise.

name: Tampere Maraton 13.9.2026
description: Tampere Marathon is a true city marathon, held in the heart of Tampere on 13 September 2026. The event offers a marathon, half marathon, 10 km race, minimarathon for the youngest members of the family, and a marathon relay for teams of four. The route runs through the city centre and alongside Tampere’s waterways, mostly on asphalt and partly on gravel paths, offering beautiful urban scenery and a challenge for runners. The start and finish area is at Tampere Stadium, which is well connected by public transport. Organised by runners, for runners, the event offers the joy of achievement to runners of all ages and abilities.
course_highlights: The route runs through the city centre and alongside Tampere’s waterways
Mostly asphalt with some gravel paths; the route has been officially measured
Two aid stations approximately every 3–4 km, with toilets at the aid stations
additional: Race office open Sat 12.9. from 16:00 to 19:00 and Sun 13.9. from 8:00 onwards at Tampere Stadium. The 10 km start is at Aleksandra Siltanen Park, approximately 2 km from the stadium; allow 20 minutes to get to the start. Changing rooms and bag storage at Tampere Stadium. Marathon pacers will run target times of 3:45 (uncertain), 4:00, 4:15, 4:30 and 5:00. A hot soup meal, juice and water will be available at the finish. Timing and results service by MyLaps Sports Service. Lead cyclists ensure the front runners have an unobstructed route. Traffic control on the course is provided in cooperation with the police. The event takes place on 13.9.2026; registration is open online; various categories and distances are available; participants are provided with race services and route information; Runner’s Card discounts are available, and participation can be transferred with a medical certificate.

name: Ruskahölkkä
distance_verbose: 7 km, 5 km, 2 km, 1 km, 0.5 km, 0.3 km, 0.1 km
description: Ruskahölkkä is a varied cross-country running event in Oulainen, offering races and distances for runners of all ages and fitness levels. The event takes place in the Honkamaja area and includes distances ranging from 0.3 km children’s races to 10 km open races, as well as fitness races. Prizes are awarded in every race category, and there are also prize draws, including a bicycle draw. Runners can use changing rooms with showers, and the event is part of Oulaisten Taru’s wide-ranging sports activities.
course_highlights: A variety of distances for children and adults, from 0.3 km to 10 km
5 km and 10 km fitness races
Changing rooms with showers for women and men
additional: Late entries are charged double. Prizes are awarded to at least the top three in each category; all participants in categories for under-12s receive a prize. Prizes are drawn among fitness race participants. All runners are entered into the bicycle draw. The event includes various distances, such as 0.1 km, 0.3 km, 0.5 km, 1 km, 2 km, 5 km and 7 km, and is a popular local event offering the chance to run in nature.

name: Hiekkojen Herruus Trail Run
description: Hiekkojen Herruus Trail Run offers fast-paced and suitably challenging routes through Kalajoki’s stunning pine forests and coastal scenery. The route follows winding pine-needle trails and includes technically challenging sections that test runners’ fitness and skills. The race is part of a two-day event that also offers an MTB race and a combined event. Welcome to experience the unique atmosphere of Kalajoki’s sandy terrain and challenge yourself!
course_highlights: Winding pine-needle trails through pine forests
Coastal scenery
Technically challenging sections
additional: Race bib distribution starts at 9:00 at the event center. Bike-washing facilities, changing rooms, showers, and a sauna are available at the race venue. During the event weekend, participants can get discounted admission to Sanifani water park (adult €14, child €8). Participation is at your own risk; valid liability insurance is recommended. The event includes trail run and MTB races, different age categories, the race-day schedule, and registration instructions. Participants can also enjoy the saunas and showers at the race venue.

name: Renforsin maraton, Kajaani
description: Renfors Marathon is a charity running event held in Kajaani on 19 September 2026. Proceeds support local youth sports. The event offers a beautiful route past Kajaani’s scenic river landscapes and landmarks, including the area near the ruins of Kajaani Castle. The start and finish area is Raatihuoneentori, and the route follows the banks of the Kajaaninjoki River. In addition to the marathon, the event includes a half marathon, a quarter marathon and children’s races for different age groups.
course_highlights: The route follows the banks of the Kajaaninjoki River
The ruins of Kajaani Castle are along the route
The route has approximately 80 m of total elevation gain and is approximately 60% firm-surface gravel road and 40% asphalt
additional: Children’s races are free, and participants receive awards. Mini-Renfors races are available for children under 8 (150 m) and over 8 (300 m), with no timekeeping. There are three aid stations along the route (3.5 km, 7.0 km and 10.5 km), offering sports drink and water. Race materials can be collected from the race office on Friday from 17:00 to 19:00 or from 9:00 on race day. Awards for the top three in each category will be presented at 15:00 in Raatihuoneentori. The Oktoberfest tent opens at 16:00. The event is a charity event supporting youth sports, and gives participants the opportunity to enjoy beautiful surroundings and a community atmosphere.

name: Kyröö-hölkkä 19.9.2026
description: Kyröö Run is a relaxed running event held in the beautiful countryside of Isokyrö. The event offers suitable distances for both joggers and faster runners, and the race also awards the unofficial Finnish Championship medals in gravel running. The start is at the Kyrö Visitor Centre, and the route runs through varied but flat terrain. Come and enjoy the joy of exercise in good company, and run where the asphalt ends!
course_highlights: The route runs through the countryside of Isokyrö over varied but flat terrain
The Jauri 15 km route includes a water station at approximately the 7 km mark
The Palonkylä 5 km route goes along Jaurintie, Taavetintie, Palonkyläntie and Perttiläntie
additional: Entry fees include water stations, refreshments at the finish, a participation prize (a jar of Sugar Daddies honey), and access to showers at Pärske Swimming Hall, 2.6 km away. Fees can also be paid using sports benefits (Smartum, Edenred, Epassi), following the instructions sent by email. Buffet dining is available at the Kyrö Visitor Centre after the event. Parking is at the yard of the Kyrönmaa Agricultural Museum. Advance registration is required, and the event includes a possible entry fee and insurance. Participants may also be photographed and filmed for the event’s marketing.

name: Ylivieska Trail Run – Meleko hyvä polokujuoksutapahtuma
description: Ylivieska Trail Run is a trail-running event held on Saturday, 19 September 2026, at the Törmälä camp centre and Rantakalla in Ylivieska. The event offers 14 km competitive races for men and women, as well as fitness and hiking categories over 1.5 km, 5 km and 11 km distances. Prizes are also available in the youth categories, and the youngest children can take part in a free stadium dash. An extended weekend at Kalajoki’s Jäkälähovi will be raffled among all participants. The event offers variety and is suitable for trail runners of different levels.
course_highlights: Trail running in the Törmälä camp centre and Rantakalla area
14 km competitive races for men and women
Fitness and hiking categories over 1.5 km, 5 km and 11 km
additional: The youth categories offer trophies and prizes. Youth category distances: boys and girls aged 16: 5 km; boys and girls aged 12: 1.5 km; boys and girls aged 9: 1.5 km. These races are free. The stadium dash for children aged 1–6 is approximately 200 metres and is free. An extended weekend at Kalajoki’s Jäkälähovi will be raffled among all participants. Various race categories, trail terrain, registration details, free events for children

name: HOKA Messilä Vertical

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Ilmoittautuminen päättyy 30.7. Hinnat viimeisen maksuportaan mukaan.

description: HOKA Messilä Vertical is a unique race in which competitors aim to accumulate the most elevation gain within a set time. The race takes place at the Messilä Ski Resort in Hollola. Participants run a 1.2 km course with approximately 90 metres of ascent and descent per lap. There are three race categories lasting 1, 2 or 4 hours, and the winner in each category is the competitor who completes the most laps. The event is open to all ages, and the atmosphere is relaxed but challenging, making it suitable for both first-timers and experienced runners.
course_highlights: A 1.2 km course with approximately 90 metres of ascent and descent per lap
The course runs mainly on a mowed ski slope and grassy areas in the event centre
The number of laps determines the result, not the total time
additional: There is a drinks station and an official support area at the event centre, where competitors may have their own support person. After their race, participants can use the sauna at the Messilä Hotel from 11:00 to 15:00 to relax. Trail shoes or shoes with studs and a coarse tread are recommended, especially in wet weather. There are no minimum or maximum age limits. The event takes place at the Messilä Ski Resort and includes the option to use the sauna and dining facilities after the race. It is aimed at fans of mountain sports and trail running who want to challenge themselves on elevation.

name: Kullervo-maraton 2026
location: Joutsenen urheilukeskus, Joutsenon, Lappeenranta, South Karelia, Finland
description: Kullervo Marathon 2026 will be held at Joutseno Sports Centre on Sunday, 20 September 2026. This traditional event offers Finland’s fastest marathon course, which is almost entirely paved and flat. The race includes a marathon, half marathon, 10 km and children’s minimarathon, making it suitable for runners of various levels. The course is well marked and has plenty of aid stations. Participants receive course support, a medal, coffee, a sweet bun and soup lunch at the race restaurant.
course_highlights: The course is almost entirely paved and practically flat, with the exception of a small climb on a connecting section
Distances are marked every 3 km with colour-coded kilometre signs
There are two aid stations along the course, approximately every 4 km; the half marathon also has one additional aid station on the first lap
additional: The race office is located at Joutseno Hall and is open on Sat 19 Sep from 17:00 to 19:00 and Sun 20 Sep from 8:30 to 17:00. Race numbers must be collected from the race office. The maximum time limit is 6 hours for the marathon; there is no time limit for the half marathon or 10 km. Changing rooms, showers and toilets are available at Joutseno Hall. Free supervised baggage storage is next to the race office. Late registration is available at the race office on Sat 19 Sep from 17:00 to 19:00 and from 8:30 on Sun 20 Sep, closing one hour before each distance starts. Payments at the race office are accepted by card or MobilePay only. Participation can be deferred to the following year with a certificate from a healthcare provider, or transferred to another person by 17 September 2026 at the latest. Registration is online, and entry fees include course support, a medal, coffee, a sweet bun and soup lunch. The marathon is for participants over 18, and no advance registration is required for the children’s minimarathon. Late registration is also available on race day, and participation can be deferred to another year with a certificate from a healthcare provider.

name: KOMIA Kyrkösjärven kierros
description: KOMIA Kyrkösjärven kierros is Seinäjoki’s legendary and popular running event, held around Kyrkösjärvi. The event venue is Kyrkösjärvi Beach and the Käpälikkö Nature Centre, where the start, finish, parking and event centre are located. The main distance is a 15.4 km route. There is also the shorter, approximately 4.3 km Pikku Kyrkkäri for young participants or as a jog, and the 400–500 m Mini Kyrkkäri for the youngest family members. The event offers a memorable running experience surrounded by nature and is open to participants across different age and competition categories.
course_highlights: 15.4 km route around Kyrkösjärvi
One water station approximately halfway along the route, offering water and sports drink
The start, finish and event centre are all at Kyrkösjärvi Beach
additional: Bib collection and registration at the event office from 9.30 to 10.45. Runners start together in a mass start. Mini Kyrkkäri starts at 11.10. Baggage storage and gear transport are available in the finish area. A café is located in the event centre. Changing facilities and toilets are in the beach changing rooms. Participants receive a commemorative prize. Littering in nature is prohibited. Participation is at your own risk; leisure-time insurance is recommended. First aid is available in the finish area and at the water stations. The event includes several distances and age groups, and registration is available online or on site. The course follows nature trails, and the event is held annually in September at Kyrkösjärvi.

name: Juutuanvaaran kymppi – polkujuoksu Inarissa 2026
location: Juutunvaaran vanha metsä, Inari, Lapland, Finland
description: Juutuanvaaran Kymppi is a new trail running event in Inari, offering scenic trails of various lengths for all runners. The route runs through the old forest of Juutuanvaara, with varied terrain from pine heath to mountain birch woodland and magnificent views of Lake Inari. The race starts on 20 September 2026 at 12:00, and participants will receive honorary prizes and commemorative medals. The event is suitable for both recreational and competitive runners, and participants will receive a race sausage and a drink.
course_highlights: 159 m elevation difference, 354 m ascent
Pine heath and mountain birch woodland
Magnificent views of Lake Inari
additional: Children’s adventure route: 0.5–1 km. Honorary prizes for the best in the main categories. Commemorative medal for all participants. The entry fee includes a race sausage and a drink. 159 m elevation difference, 354 m ascent, pine heath, mountain birch woodland, views of Lake Inari

name: Petzl Nuuksio Night Trail
description: Petzl Nuuksio Night Trail is an autumn night trail-running event held in the dark on forest trails in Nuuksio National Park. The event starts from Luukki Outdoor Recreation Centre in Espoo on 25.9.2026 and offers a route of approximately 13 kilometres, challenging runners amid nature. There is a dedicated category for non-binary participants, and free gear storage is available. A headlamp is mandatory because the route runs through a dark forest.
course_highlights: Approximately 13 km of trail running on Nuuksio’s autumn forest trails
Run in a dark forest; a headlamp is mandatory
Event centre and start at Luukki Outdoor Recreation Centre, Luukintie 33
additional: The race office is near the start and finish, where runners can collect their race numbers and register on the day. The organiser does not rent headlamps, so participants must bring their own. Timing is handled by an electronic timing app, and race numbers must be clearly attached at chest height. The maximum time allowed is 2.5 hours. Free gear storage is available near the race office on event day. Cash is not accepted, including for on-the-day registration. 13 km trail run in forest, mandatory headlamp, race categories including a mixed gender series, registration and timing details, event facilities including changing rooms, showers, sauna, and parking.

name: 1. Full Moon Backyard Ultra Kymi
description: Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon in which competitors run a 6.706-kilometre course within one hour. The race continues as long as multiple runners can complete a lap in under an hour, and the winner is the person who runs one lap more than the others. The course is either a loop or an out-and-back route, and the starting area remains the same throughout the race. There is no predetermined time limit, making the race particularly challenging and exciting. Backyard Ultra events are organised collaboratively in Finland, and the sport is actively being developed.
course_highlights: The course is a 6.706 km loop or out-and-back route
Each lap starts on the hour
The race continues as long as runners can complete a lap in under an hour
additional: A start warning is given 3, 2 and 1 minutes before the start. Competitors may not leave the course during a lap, except to use the toilet. Competitors must be in the starting area at the start, and the starting area remains the same throughout the race. Outside assistance and aids such as poles are not permitted. Slower runners must give way to faster runners. Timing lap times is optional. The event includes trail running on forest paths, and participants can use toilets, showers and shelter areas. The start is at Alakyläntie 67 in Kotka, and the course is approximately 6.7 km per lap.

name: Vihteljärven ympärijuoksu - 67.
description: The Vihteljärvi Circuit Run is Satakunta’s oldest continuously held annual running event, organized since 1960. The event offers a 6.5-kilometer race in several age groups, as well as a fun run without timing. There are also children’s events over shorter distances. The race takes place at Vihteljärvi School in Kankaanpää and offers participants a traditional, community-oriented running experience in a scenic setting.
course_highlights: 6.5 km race in several age groups
Children’s events over distances of 0.2–1 km
Satakunta’s oldest continuously held annual running event
additional: Registration and payment at the event venue from 10:00 onward; payment by cash, MobilePay, or ePass. Participants in the lake circuit can take part without timing from 10:00 onward. Children’s events start at 10:30 and the circuit run at 12:00. The top three in the competitive events receive prizes; every child participant receives a prize. A smart TV will be raffled among participants in the lake circuit. The event starts at Laviantie 1035 and also includes children’s events, with prizes for all participants.

name: Kiehimänjoen juoksu 2026
description: Kiehimänjoki Run is a running event being held for the fifth time in Paltamo, offering a marathon, half marathon, 10K fun run and children’s race. The event starts on Saturday, 26 September 2026, at 11:00. The race centre is at Kotolinna, where runners can use the facilities, dine, enjoy the saunas and stay overnight. The courses are officially measured, and all categories are timed. After the run, runners can book a recovery massage. On-site registration is available for an additional fee for adults.
course_highlights: The 42.2 km marathon and 21.1 km half marathon are officially measured and approved by SUL.
There are three aid stations along the course, offering sports drink, water, raisins and pickles.
After finishing, runners can use the showers, sauna and hot tub, and enjoy a warm soup meal.
additional: On-site registration costs an additional €5 for adults. After the run, runners can book a 20-minute massage (€20). The race centre at Kotolinna has changing rooms, showers, a sauna and a hot tub. ePassi and fitness vouchers are accepted at the venue. Accommodation is available at Kotomo. Prices excluding breakfast: single room €80, double room €120; breakfast €14. The event route includes town streets and possibly rural areas; registration is available online and on site; food, sauna and massage services are offered; several distances are available for runners of different levels.

name: Suojuoksun elämyskisa
description: The Swamp Run Experience Race is a unique running event held at Kauklaisten Ojassuo. The event gives runners the opportunity to challenge themselves and enjoy a different kind of running experience surrounded by nature. There are several route options of different lengths, suitable for both experienced runners and first-timers. Join us to enjoy the joy of running and a sense of community!
course_highlights: The run takes place in the scenic natural surroundings of Kauklaisten Ojassuo
Several route options: 1.4 km, 2.7 km, 4.1 km and 5.5 km
The event offers a unique running experience for both experienced runners and first-timers
additional: Registration takes place on site. The entry fee is €12 (€10 with a runner’s card) and includes raffle prizes and a medal. The race has categories for different route lengths, including M-General 5.5 km and T15 1.350 km. The event includes different types of running, such as road and trail running, but more detailed information about arrangements and participation is not available.

name: Lampaloppet 2026
description: Lampaloppet 2026 will take place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, at Lamminaho in Pyhäjärvi. The route winds through the scenery of Honkavuori and introduces runners to Ahto’s historic sites. The event offers a suitable challenge for both competitive runners and more casual participants. The competitive categories are timed, but there is also an untimed fun run where participants can move at their own pace. Participants can use the water stations, washing facilities and sauna, and receive a Lampaloppet neck gaiter.
course_highlights: The route winds through the scenery of Honkavuori
A chance to explore Ahto’s historic sites
Water stations at approximately 5 km and 10 km, and at the finish
additional: The entry fee includes a marked route, timing in the competitive categories, water stations, washing facilities and sauna, and a Lampaloppet neck gaiter. The top three finishers in the competitive categories will receive prizes, and an Ooni pizza oven will be raffled among all participants. The fun run is an untimed distance of the participant’s choice. The event also includes the Honkavuori Stair Community and a stair relay competition, which will be held in July 2026. Entry fees vary, and the event offers the opportunity to compete both individually and as a team.

name: 58. Vihtijärvihölkkä
price_range: 15 eur (enakko), 20 eur (paikan päällä) for half marathon; 10 eur (enakko), 15 eur (paikan päällä) for 10 km; 4 eur (enakko), 5 eur (paikan päällä) for 9-13 sarjat; 10 eur (enakko), 15 eur (paikan päällä) for other series
description: Vihtijärvihölkkä is a long-running running event offering competitors the chance to take part in a half marathon, a 10-kilometre run and shorter distances. The routes pass through varied terrain, with several water stations serving runners along the way. The event is open to different age groups and categories and is held in the Vihtijärvi area. The race has been held 58 times, reflecting its popularity and tradition among local residents.
course_highlights: Water stations on the half-marathon route approximately every 3–3.5 km
A water station at the 5 km mark on the 10 km route
Varied terrain and several distance and category options
additional: Race numbers must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start. On-site registration is possible up to one hour before the start of the relevant category. There are several water stations along the route, and payment can also be made using MobilePay code 27789. Participation is free for Vihtijärven Uhka members in the 9–17-year-old categories. Several distances, registration instructions, start schedules and route details are available; outdoor terrain in the Vihtijärvi area; free participation for children aged 9–17; an event medal can be purchased after the race.

name: Voimaa Metsästä
description: Voimaa Metsästä is a trail running and outdoor activity event in Tampere, held on 27.9.2026 at Kauppi Sports Park. The event offers varied routes over distances of 2–21 kilometres, suitable for beginners and experienced trail runners alike. Taking part supports charity, as the event proceeds will be donated to Tays’s new psychiatric hospital for children and young people. The routes are well marked and varied, offering all participants the tranquillity of nature and the joy of exercise.
course_highlights: Varied terrain, mostly on trails
Pirunvuori, the highest point in the Kauppi area, with about 50 metres of elevation gain
Two aid stations along the route, with course marshals on the trails
additional: The entry fee includes soup lunch and refreshments at the aid stations. This year, participants will also receive an event shirt, which can be collected when picking up their race number. The event also has untimed hiking categories over 6 km and 12 km. Travel by public transport or on foot/by bike is recommended, as parking is limited. Registration closes 60 minutes before the start, and entry fees increase by €5 after the advance registration period ends. The routes range from 2 to 21 km. The event raises funds for child and adolescent psychiatry; participation and donations support child psychiatry in Tampere.

name: Loimaan Lenkki
description: Loimaan Lenkki is an autumn running event held in the centre of Loimaa. There are four distances to choose from: 1.2 km, 2.4 km, 5.2 km and 10.4 km, making it suitable for a wide range of runners. The start is at Viljavarastontie 4, and the event offers a great opportunity to get active and enjoy a sense of community. Registration is open, and the event is organised by Loimaan Seudun Nuorkauppakamari.
course_highlights: Four distances: 1.2 km, 2.4 km, 5.2 km and 10.4 km
Start at Viljavarastontie 4, Loimaa
The event takes place in the centre of Loimaa
additional: Discounted prices are available for groups of at least 8 people and Junior Chamber members: €12 (10 km) / €6 (5 km). Start times for the shorter distances (1.2 km and 2.4 km) are at 12:30. The event also includes a family-friendly mini run and offers an opportunity to take part in community exercise. Participants can choose a race distance to suit their fitness and preferences.

name: KOMIA Esi-Talvijuoksusarja
description: The KOMIA Pre-Winter Running Series is a six-part winter running series that gives runners of all levels the opportunity to test their fitness and track their progress. The fast, flat routes start at Pajuluoma School and offer 2 km, 5 km and 10 km distances. The series begins with the Pre-Winter Run in early October and continues into spring. The top runners are rewarded at the end of the series, and the races are suitable for recreational and competitive runners alike.
course_highlights: Fast, flat 2 km, 5 km and 10 km routes starting at Pajuluoma School
Routes officially measured in October 2024
A six-part winter running series starting in October and continuing into spring
additional: The series offers a season pass that allows entry to all six events. There are also age categories for children (2 km), and the runner card gives a discount. The routes start at Pajuluoma School and are officially measured. The top runners are rewarded at the end of the series. A variety of trail and running events, registration information and series information.

description: Keurusselkä Autumn Run is a varied autumn event set in the beautiful surroundings of Keuruu, offering trail running and mountain biking. Trail runners can choose between two distances, 6.4 km and 12 km, while mountain bikers have several distances in different categories, including children’s and e-bike categories. The event also features children’s runs and the option to enjoy the hotel spa as part of the entry fee. The routes pass through the terrain around Resort Keurusselkä and Montosvuori, with hill running and technically varied trails. Participants can also enjoy special offers at the hotel restaurant on event day.
course_highlights: Trail runs of 6.4 km and 12 km through the terrain around Keurusselkä and Montosvuori
The mountain bike route includes technically easy outdoor trails and trail sections
Mountain biking features steep climbs and fast descents on Montosvuori
additional: Start and finish at Keurusselkä Resort. The entry fee includes use of the hotel spa. There is a water station along the route, and participants may set up their own aid stations. Payment when collecting the race number is by cash or MobilePay. The hotel restaurant has special offers on event day. Mountain biking has categories for different age groups and e-bikes. Children can sign up for their run on site. Trail running and MTB routes, a children’s run, and spa access included in the entry fee; the event takes place in the terrain around Keurusselkä and Montosvuori.

name: Visahölkkä
price_range: 12 euroa aikuiset, 6 euroa nuoret ja lapset

tiers.description: Aikuiset 12 euroa ennakkoon Visan tilille tai paikanpäällä.

description: Visahölkkä is a traditional running event held in the rural surroundings of Ojakkala on the first Sunday in October. The event has been organized since 2007, and participation has settled at 30–50 runners. The event has grown into a significant international gathering, with more than 500 participants from countries including Russia, Estonia, Sweden, England and Kenya. Through cooperation between the City of Orimattila and local village associations, the event has been carried forward one year at a time.

The event brings together recreational runners, juniors, and the national elite—an event for everyone who loves running, where you can challenge yourself in a 10,000-metre track race. Kansallinen Kymppi offers a unique opportunity to run an official 10,000-metre track race, and the evening culminates in a contest between the national elite.

The route passes through Pikisaari, Hietasaari, Toppilansaari, Möljä Bridge, Toppila Beach, Merijali Beach, Patosilta and Ainola Park, finishing at Raatin Stadium. On Saturday, September 20, you can take part in the marathon (42.195 km), half marathon (21.1 km), 10K (10 km), 5K (5 km timed run), Aalto Walk (5 km untimed walk/run), or the children’s run (1K/600 m).

name: Kullervo Marathon
description: The Kullervo Marathon 2025 will take place in Joutseno on 21 September 2025. The event is known for its fast course, where several Finnish records, domestic season bests and personal records have been set. For example, last September Ole Halonen ran the men’s domestic season best in Joutseno, with a time of 2:24:26.

The race has several categories: girls/boys under 12 years, 1.5 km; under 14 years, 2.5 km; and adult categories, 14 km and mountain bike, 28 km. name: 55. Pirkan Hölkkä 5.10.2025
description:
A jewel of the running season, the icing on the cake: this long-distance running event, held mainly on trails, takes place every year on the first Sunday in October.

The 33-kilometre route from Valkeakoski to Tampere runs along a varied mix of fitness trails, forest roads and trails. Around five kilometres of the route are on asphalt. In addition to the running categories, you can take part in a walking category, which is not timed. The event is organised jointly by Tampereen Taivaltajat ry and Valkeakosken Retkeilijät ry.

Pirkan Hölkkä dates back to 1970. The route has largely remained as it is today. In recent years, the average number of participants has been around 1,000–1,500.
additional:
You can choose from the age categories Women’s Open, N40, N50, Men’s Open, M40, M50 and M60. The start is at the Sahara sports field in Valkeakoski (Tallikatu 11), where the starting gun will sound at 9:30 on Sunday morning. Late registration at the start is available from 8:00 to 9:00.

The event uses gun time, measured from the starting gun until you cross the finish line. At the start, you can choose a position near the start line according to your target time.

The first 3 km of the race are on streets. For the next 3 km, the route follows the fitness trail in the recreational area as far as Leppäjärventie. After that, the route to Rutajärvi (11 km from the start) consists of varied forest trails and a short section of gravel road. The 3.5 km stretch between Rutajärvi and Vähä-Kausjärvi is on forest roads. Of the 5 km between Vähä-Kausjärvi and Taivalpirtti, the first part is on forest roads, followed by forest trails; after crossing Savontie, the route returns to gravel roads.
From Taivalpirtti onward, the route alternates between gravel roads and forest trails until it reaches the recreational trail around Suolijärvi. The final 3 km follow a gravel-surfaced recreational trail between Hervanta and Koivistonkylä. This section still has a few climbs that will test Finnish grit.

The Pirkan Hölkkä route is marked with blue flagging tape, directional arrows and kilometre signs. The organisers have aimed to include as many forest trails as possible. There are six refreshment stations along the route.

The finish is in Nirva, Tampere, in the grounds of Tampere Adult Education Centre (Kurssikeskuksenkatu 11). Paid bus transport to the start is available from the finish area and Tampere city centre, both in the morning before the start and in the afternoon after you finish. You can include transport and the soup lunch sold at the finish area in your entry fee by selecting these add-ons in our online store.

name: Pirkan Kieppi 5.10.2025
description:
The jewel of the running season and the icing on the cake, Pirkan Hölkkä is a long-distance running event held mostly on trails. It takes place every year on the first Sunday in October. Together with TU38, we are organizing the much-requested shorter distance, the 14 km Pirkan Kieppi.

Pirkan Kieppi starts at the Pirkan Hölkkä finish area, in the courtyard of TAKK’s Nirva campus, at 11:30. On-site late registration is open from 10:00 to 11:00.
additional:
The route continues via Lahdesjärvi to Vuores, where it winds through the beautiful scenery of this neighbourhood. It then joins the traditional Pirkan Hölkkä route at the Vormisto aid station, from where runners continue to the finish together with the full-distance participants.

Pirkan Kieppi has two open categories, women (N) and men (M). Timing is based on gun time, from the starting gun to crossing the finish line. At the start, you can choose a spot near the start line according to your target time.
